Utah is home to Pando, a colony of about 47,000 quaking aspen trees that all share a single root system. Pando is one of the largest single organisms by mass on Earth, but ecologists are worried that its growth is declining in part because of grazing by animals. The ecologists say that strong fences could prevent deer from eating young trees and help Pando start thriving again.
According to the text, why are ecologists worried about Pando?
A. It isn't growing at the same rate it used to.
B. It isn't producing young trees anymore.
C. It can't grow into new areas because it is blocked by fences.
D. Its root system can't support many more new trees.

The following text is adapted from a 1913 novel. The narrator has just arrived at a farm for the summer.
The house stood at the end of a long lane, half hidden by lilacs that had been left to grow wild. Paint curled from the shutters, and the porch sagged at one corner, yet every window had been washed until it shone, and a jar of fresh daisies stood on the sill of the kitchen.
Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
A. It describes a building and then explains why it was abandoned.
B. It presents a problem and then proposes a solution to it.
C. It notes signs of neglect and then signs of care.
D. It compares two houses that the narrator has lived in.

In 2019, researchers studying octopuses found that the animals change color while asleep. The researchers observed that the shifts in color followed a regular cycle, similar to the cycle of active sleep in humans, during which most dreaming occurs. The researchers caution, however, that it is not yet possible to know whether octopuses experience anything like human dreams.
Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
A. Octopuses dream in the same way that humans do.
B. Octopuses show a sleep pattern that resembles one in humans, but its meaning is uncertain.
C. Researchers have learned to read the dreams of octopuses from their colors.
D. Octopuses change color only when they are asleep.

Many early photographers were also skilled painters. Because exposures took several minutes, they could not capture motion, so they arranged their subjects with the same careful attention to balance and light that they had once given to a canvas.
As used in the text, what does the word "arranged" most nearly mean?
A. scheduled
B. adapted
C. settled
D. positioned

Bees can be trained to recognize the scent of certain chemicals. In one study, honeybees learned to stick out their tongues when they smelled explosives, a response that researchers could detect with a camera. ______ some scientists believe trained bees could one day help find hidden landmines.
Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
A. As a result,
B. However,
C. For instance,
D. In contrast,

The architect Zaha Hadid was known for buildings full of sweeping curves. Before she became famous for her ______ she spent years designing projects that were never built.
Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
A. buildings
B. buildings,
C. buildings;
D. buildings:

A city replaced the asphalt on several streets with a lighter-colored surface that reflects more sunlight. On a hot afternoon, the temperature of the new surface was measured at 10 degrees Celsius lower than the temperature of nearby asphalt. City officials hope the change will make summers in the neighborhood more comfortable.
Which finding, if true, would most directly support the officials' hope?
A. The lighter surface costs more to install than asphalt does.
B. Asphalt lasts longer than the lighter surface.
C. Air temperatures on streets with the lighter surface were lower than on nearby asphalt streets.
D. Drivers did not notice any difference between the two surfaces.

The poet Gwendolyn Brooks often wrote about ordinary people in her Chicago neighborhood. Rather than describing grand events, her poems focus on small moments, such as a mother cooking dinner or children playing on a street corner. Critics have praised the way these poems give dignity to everyday life.
What is the main purpose of the text?
A. To argue that Brooks's poems are difficult to understand
B. To explain how Brooks became a famous poet
C. To compare Brooks's poems with those of other Chicago writers
D. To describe a focus of Brooks's poetry and how it has been received

The students who planted the school garden ______ surprised when the first tomatoes appeared after only six weeks.
Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
A. were
B. was
C. is
D. has been

For centuries, historians assumed that medieval people rarely bathed. Recent research tells a different story: records from many medieval towns describe public bathhouses that were busy and popular, and some cities had dozens of them.
Based on the text, what can most reasonably be inferred about the historians' assumption?
A. It was based on the records of public bathhouses.
B. It was not supported by evidence from many medieval towns.
C. It has been confirmed by recent research.
D. It applied only to people who lived in cities.

Sea otters often float on their backs and use a rock to crack open the shells of clams and sea urchins. Some otters keep a favorite rock tucked in a fold of skin under their arm and use it again and again. ______ researchers consider sea otters one of the few marine mammals that use tools.
Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
A. Nevertheless,
B. Instead,
C. For this reason,
D. Similarly,

The novelist described the old library as a place where time seemed to slow down: dust drifted in the light from the tall windows, the clocks ticked softly, and readers turned pages without hurry.
Which choice best describes the function of the details about dust, clocks, and readers?
A. They explain why the library was rarely visited.
B. They suggest that the library needed repairs.
C. They show that the narrator found the library boring.
D. They help create a calm and unhurried mood.
